meta.title: Celestial test vectors for scripts/celestial-core.js (reduced fixture)
meta.note: Reduced copy of the development vector file (69 vectors, 726 kB): the 11 named vectors, 12 of its 48 modern and 6 of its 10 ancient ones, each with the blocks spec, ephem and rigorous. The full file, which also holds Swiss Ephemeris and Skyfield blocks and the measured accuracy tables, was used in development: 69 vectors, 6,900 checks, 0 failures.

ephem.role: PRIMARY expected values (block 'ephem'); XEphem's libastro routines with their own Delta T model

pyswisseph.role: second library (block 'swisseph'); own Delta T (Stephenson-Morrison-Hohenkerk 2016 model)

pyerfa.role: sidereal time, precession (IAU 1976/2006, Vondrak long-term), galactic transform

astropy.role: galactic/ecliptic cross-check of the anchor table; Planck18 cosmology

astronomy-engine.role: cross-check for modern dates only (NOT used at 600 BC: its Moon is 0.35 deg off there)

PyMeeus.role: source-code cross-check of the lunar term tables only

conventions.time: All inputs are Universal Time (UT1 ~ UTC). jd_ut is the Julian Day in UT. TT = UT + Delta T.
conventions.calendar: 'gregorian' or 'julian' as stated per vector; years are astronomical (0 = 1 BC, -592 = 593 BC).
conventions.longitudes: Sun/Moon ecliptic longitude and latitude are APPARENT geocentric, referred to the true equinox and ecliptic of date.
conventions.ra_dec: true equator and equinox of date, geocentric.
conventions.sidereal_time: gmst = Greenwich mean sidereal time; gast = apparent (gmst + equation of the equinoxes); last = gast + east longitude.
conventions.alt_az: airless (no refraction), azimuth from north through east; Moon alt/az are topocentric (parallax applied), sea level.
conventions.stars: fixed J2000 directions (no proper motion); spec values include precession + nutation but not aberration (<= 0.006 deg).
conventions.elong_lon_deg: (Moon longitude - Sun longitude) mod 360: 0 new, 90 first quarter, 180 full, 270 last quarter.
conventions.phase_names: New/First Quarter/Full/Last Quarter when elong_lon is within 6 deg of 0/90/180/270; otherwise Waxing Crescent, Waxing Gibbous, Waning Gibbous, Waning Crescent.
conventions.ephem_ecliptic: PyEphem ecliptic coordinates were derived from its apparent g_ra/g_dec with the true obliquity of date from Swiss Ephemeris.
conventions.ephem_illuminated_fraction: Moon.phase/100 (Moon.moon_phase is NOT used: it is wrong by several percent at 600 BC).

anchors.label: Sagittarius A*
anchors.distance_note: GRAVITY 2019: 8178 +-13(stat) +-22(sys) pc; GRAVITY 2021/22: 8277 +-9(stat) pc. Quote as 'about 8.2 kpc = 26,700 light-years (+-300 ly between recent measurements)'.

anchors.label: Vela pulsar (PSR B0833-45 = PSR J0835-4510)
anchors.distance_note: VLBI parallax 3.4 +-0.2 mas -> 293 (+19,-17) pc (arXiv:astro-ph/0302374v3); the journal version is usually cited as 287 (+19,-17) pc (not opened here). Quote as 'about 290 pc = 940-960 light-years (+-60 ly)'.

anchors.label: Cygnus X-1
anchors.distance_note: Miller-Jones et al. 2021: 2.22 (+0.18,-0.17) kpc; Reid et al. 2011: 1.86 (+0.12,-0.11) kpc. Quote as 'about 2.2 kpc = 7,200 light-years (published values 6,100-7,200 ly)'.

anchors.label: Pleiades (M45); position of Alcyone (eta Tau), the brightest member
anchors.distance_note: VLBI: 136.2 +-1.2 pc (Melis et al. 2014); Hipparcos gave 120.2 +-1.5 pc (now regarded as too short). Quote as 'about 136 pc = 444 light-years'.
anchors.position_source: general knowledge (Hipparcos); matches PyEphem's built-in star catalogue entry for Alcyone to 0.1 arcsec

anchors.label: Polaris (alpha Ursae Minoris)
anchors.distance_note: Hipparcos 7.54 +-0.11 mas -> 132.6 pc (433 ly); Gaia DR2 (companion Polaris B) 7.292 +-0.028 mas -> 137.2 pc (447 ly); HST 6.26 +-0.24 mas -> 160 pc; Turner et al. 99 +-2 pc. Quote as 'about 430-450 light-years; published estimates span 320-520 ly'.
anchors.position_source: general knowledge (Hipparcos); matches PyEphem's built-in star catalogue to 0.2 arcsec

anchors.distance_note: HST Cepheids: 761 +-11 kpc (Li et al. 2021). Quote as 'about 2.5 million light-years (+-0.1)'.

scale_objects.label: Moon
scale_objects.note: 384,400 km is the conventional mean (semi-major axis 384,399 km); 385,000.56 km is the constant term of the distance series used in the spec; perigee/apogee extremes about 356,400-406,700 km.

scale_objects.label: Sun
scale_objects.note: 1 au = 149,597,870.7 km exactly (IAU 2012 definition); light takes 499.0 s = 8 min 19 s.

scale_objects.label: Cosmic microwave background, last-scattering surface
scale_objects.note: Three different numbers: light-travel time 13.79 billion yr (so 'light-travel distance' 13.79 billion ly); PRESENT (comoving) distance of the emitting matter about 45.3 billion ly; distance of that matter WHEN the light left about 41.5 million ly. Computed with astropy.cosmology.Planck18; Planck 2018 Table 2 gives z*=1089.92+-0.25, r*=144.43+-0.26 Mpc, 100*theta*=1.04110+-0.00031 (-> 13,873 Mpc), age 13.797+-0.023 Gyr (13.787+-0.020 with BAO).

tolerances.how_to_use: For every vector: (1) values under 'spec' are produced by the Python reference implementation of the spec; a correct port must reproduce them to 'vs_spec'. (2) values under 'ephem' (PyEphem 4.2.1, native) are the independent expected values; the port must agree within 'vs_ephem' for the vector's era. (3) 'rigorous' holds Swiss Ephemeris positions evaluated at the spec's own TT plus an ERA-based sidereal time; use 'vs_rigorous' to test geometry without Delta T model noise. For alt/az compare the great-circle distance between the two directions with the 'direction' tolerance (azimuth alone is ill-conditioned near the zenith); if you compare components, use alt tolerance = direction tolerance and az tolerance = direction tolerance / cos(alt).
tolerances.era_rule: era = 'ancient' if jd_ut < 1600000 (before about 330 BC) else 'modern'

vs_ephem.why_ancient_is_loose: At 700-500 BC PyEphem's Delta T differs from the Espenak-Meeus value used by the spec by 300-715 s; the Moon moves 0.55 arcsec per second, so the two disagree by up to 0.12 deg in the Moon's longitude although both lunar theories agree to 0.012 deg at equal TT. PyEphem's star precession is also off by about 0.013 deg at 593 BC.

bright_limb.note: Bright limb of the Moon as the observer sees it, from PyEphem 4.2.1 (pressure 0): the ten cases of the critique run with a Sun-Moon elongation of 20 to 160 degrees. limb_from_zenith_deg is the formula of the core applied to the altitudes and azimuths PyEphem gives; q_minus_chi_deg is the independent definition, parallactic angle minus position angle of the bright limb, from apparent topocentric right ascension and declination. The Moon altitude is topocentric.

extra.note: Further reference values from PyEphem 4.2.1, made for the committed test: equinoxes and solstices (next_vernal_equinox and its three siblings), and sunrise and sunset of the centre of the Sun at -0.8333 degrees with no air (previous_rising and next_setting from local mean noon, horizon -0.8333, pressure 0, use_center). A null instant means PyEphem reported that the Sun stays up or stays down. Years in date_ut and in the labels are written as historians write them (593 BC).
